study type: randomized comparative analysis and prospective study
outcome: Neonatal complications (birth asphyxia, meconium aspiration syndrome)
cohort: 240 pregnant women (120 with meconium-stained amniotic fluid and 120 with clear amniotic fluid)
finding: Meconium-stained amniotic fluid was associated with an increased rate of caesarean section and operative vaginal deliveries, lower Apgar scores, and a higher incidence of neonatal complications, particularly birth asphyxia.
